scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance event on router16, all Campus 1 PCs
(PC5-14) report intermittent reachability to Campus 2 and the
backbone. The mswitch0 SVI gateways still respond, but anything
beyond router16 is unreachable. Diagnose.

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router16 ospfd
Mechanism: router16 is the L3 edge between mswitch0 (Campus 1
  multilayer switch) and the backbone (router7/router8/etc.).
  With router16's ospfd dead, mswitch0 loses its OSPF
  neighbor for the backbone direction; Campus 1's only
  uplink stops advertising and learning. Inside Campus 1
  routing continues (mswitch0 ↔ access switches) but no
  off-campus traffic.
Localization: router16
Root cause: ospfd not running on router16
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on router16 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on router16" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on router16

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on router16. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
During the maintenance event, router16's FRR configuration was wiped. The
device now boots with a bare FRR stub (hostname only, no routing process, no
interface statements). As a direct consequence, the ospfd daemon is not
running on router16 at all ("ospfd is not running" confirmed via vtysh).

The affected subsystem is OSPF — router16 is the sole Layer-3 bridge between
two OSPF segments: the mswitch0 uplink segment (10.2.2.0/24) and the backbone
link to router7 (172.30.1.0/24). Because router16 no longer participates in
OSPF, both adjacencies fail to form. mswitch0 shows zero OSPF neighbors and
its routing table contains only its four directly connected prefixes
(172.16.10/20/30.0/24 and 10.2.2.0/24) — no backbone routes whatsoever.
Router7 confirms the same gap: it has three healthy Full adjacencies to the
rest of the backbone but no neighbor on 172.30.1.0/24, so it has zero routes
to any Campus 1 VLAN subnet. End-to-end, Campus 1 PCs can reach their mswitch0
SVI gateways (the directly connected hop is unaffected) but all traffic
destined beyond router16 is black-holed there: router16 has no route to the
campus VLANs and the backbone has no route back to them.

Root cause: the maintenance event cleared router16's FRR running configuration,
stopping ospfd and removing all OSPF network statements.

Corrective fix: restore the OSPF process on router16 with both segments in
area 0:
  router ospf
    network 10.2.2.0/24 area 0
    network 172.30.1.0/24 area 0
  exit
Reload/commit the config, verify ospfd starts ("show ip ospf"), and confirm
Full adjacencies form with mswitch0 and router7 before closing the ticket.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies router16 as the affected device.
Agent explicitly identifies ospfd/OSPF as the affected component, stating ospfd is not running and the OSPF configuration is missing on router16.
The agent explicitly instructs restoring the router ospf process with the two network statements and committing the config, which (along with starting FRR/ospfd) will restore OSPF and adjacencies.

The investigation log fully supports the agent's claims: router16's running-config lacks any OSPF config and 'show ip ospf' reports 'ospfd is not running', mswitch0 has no learned backbone routes, and router7 lacks the neighbor on the router16 link. The writeup's causal chain (config wiped → ospfd down → adjacencies fail → campus loses off-site routes) follows logically and the checks performed are sufficient to localize and prescribe the fix.
